stem:
Mehak prepares three mixtures for class: sugar stirred completely into lemonade until nothing separate can be seen; roasted peanuts mixed with raisins and curry leaves; and mustard oil poured onto a bowl of water so a clear layer floats on top.

In a uniform mixture the components are spread so evenly that they cannot be seen separately.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: The lemonade is a uniform mixture; the peanut mix and the oil-on-water are non-uniform mixtures.
The peanut mix is a uniform mixture because the pieces are all dry snacks.
Oil floating as a layer on water is a uniform mixture.
The lemonade is a compound because two substances are present together.

teacher.key_rationale: Fully dissolved lemonade shows no separate parts (uniform). Peanuts with raisins show separate pieces, and oil on water shows layers (non-uniform). A mixture is not a compound just because two substances sit together.
